title: KPI Runway Decision Playlist and Preflight Matrix
content:
Purpose:
A compact, actionable KPI runway and decision-playlist to support feature launches (pilot -> canary -> ramp). This sheet combines the measurable KPIs, threshold decision rules, owner runbook actions, and a short contingency playlist so product, SRE, and CS can execute fast when metrics deviate.

Summary snapshot (one-line):
- Target launch window: pilot 2 weeks, canary 72 hours, ramp 14 days
- Primary stability SLO: p95 latency <= 380ms, error-rate < 0.25%
- Business signal: token usage growth + user retention by cohort day7 >= 12% vs control

KPI definitions and measurement (owners + query hints):
1) Latency (p95) — owner: Noah Kim (SRE)
   - Measurement: p95 request latency across prod-route /model/generate, 5m rolling
   - Query hint: observability-dashboard > latency > env=prod, route=generate
   - Green: <= 380ms, Yellow: 380-520ms, Red: >520ms
2) Error-rate (5m) — owner: Arjun Patel (Backend)
   - Measurement: % requests with 5xx or retriable errors, 1m/5m buckets
   - Green: <0.25%, Yellow: 0.25-1.0%, Red: >1.0%
3) Cost per 1k tokens (ops) — owner: Maya Chen (Product Ops)
   - Measurement: infra cost / produced tokens (7-day rolling)
   - Thresholds used for scale decisions: target <$0.45 per 1k tokens
4) Quality regression (evals) — owner: Lena Rodriguez (Applied ML)
   - Measurement: prompt-set A/B delta on precision & hallucination score (daily)
   - Red trigger: >3% drop in primary metric vs baseline or >7% drop in any safety metric
5) User signal (cohort D7 retention uplift) — owner: Sofia Martinez (CS/Analytics)
   - Measurement: D7 retention vs control, 95% CI
   - Green: >= +12% uplift, Yellow: +5-12%, Red: <+5%

Decision-playlist (Go/No-Go tree - condensed):
- Checkpoint 0 (pilot start): all green or no-red on 3 core KPIs (latency, error-rate, quality) -> proceed to canary. If any red: hold pilot, run root-cause runbook (see actions).
- Canary entrance: throttled traffic at 1% -> monitor 0-24h intensively.
  - If latency or error-rate goes Yellow for >30m or increases trending up: pause ramp for 2x window and run mitigation steps.
  - If any Red persists >15m during canary: rollback to previous model variant.
- Ramp decision (after 72h of canary): evaluate 72h summary across KPIs and user signal.
  - Pass -> 25% ramp, then 50% after 24h, full after 7 days of stability.
  - Fail -> trigger partial rollback to safe model or reduce traffic until resolved.

Owner-runbook: quick actions by trigger level
- Yellow (action within 1 hour): increase logging-level for affected components; scale replica count by +20% in dedicated pool; notify #prod-ops-alerts; start incident doc (temporary).
- Red (action immediate): flip canary traffic to 0%, initiate rollback PR, engage on-call SRE, open a triage doc and loop legal if user-data exposure suspected.

Preflight checklist (to be green before pilot):
- Infra: dedicated GPU pool reservation confirmed (infra PR merged, capacity ok) [owner: Noah Kim]
- Observability: dashboards and alerts created with threshold alerting (pager/Slack) [owner: Arjun Patel]
- Model: version pinned, quantization profile validated, fallback model tested [owner: Lena Rodriguez]
- Product: feature flags created, user cohort selection defined, comms plan for beta customers [owner: Maya Chen]
- CS & Support: canned responses drafted, triage runbook distributed, ops on-call scheduled [owner: Sofia Martinez]
- Security & Legal: data retention & KMS checks signed off for private data (if applicable) [owner: Legal Security SME]

Contingency playlist (short):
- Soft degrade: enable reduced-context mode + aggressive prefix cache (cuts token cost and latency)
- Model fallback: route 10% traffic to smaller model for comparison (split test)
- Traffic freeze: immediately set api-key throttle to current value to stop growth while debugging

Minimal observability queries to run during canary (share with SRE):
- p95 latency by region and model_variant, 5m window
- error-rate 1m and endpoint breakdown (client errors vs infra errors)
- tail queue length and GPU utilization per node
- token-per-request distribution and cost spikes
- sample outputs (10/day) to quality dashboard for manual review

Rollout timeline artifact (sample):
- Day -7: final preflight sign-offs, infra canary deploy ready
- Day 0: pilot begin (limited partners)
- Day 7: pilot summary, decision for canary
- Day 9: canary start (1% traffic)
- Day 12: canary 72h review -> ramp to 25% if green
- Day 19: 50% intermediate, monitor
- Day 26: full ramp if stable

Communication script (short)
- If green: "Canary stable at 72h; ramping to 25% for broader visibility. No action required from teams other than monitoring."
- If yellow: "Observed elevated latency/error-rate during canary; holding ramp and investigating. SRE assigned: @NoahKim."
- If red: "Canary paused and rolled back. Incident team paged; triage doc: <link>. Do not re-enable traffic until incident owner clears."

Appendix: quick links and quick wins
- Quick wins to reduce p95: enable KV-cache on frequent prefixes; enable CPU-side batching for small requests; tune batch size limiter to prefer latency.
- Quick links: Confluence preflight template, JIRA board PRODOPS, infra PR bundle (linked above).

Notes and open questions:
- Evaluate automated rollback policy if model quality drops but latency remains green (who owns customer-visible regression?).
- Need a lightweight way to collect 50 manual output checks per day for hallucination signal; propose a short sampling lambda.

Document history:
- Drafted by Maya Chen 2024-11-08
- Reviewed by Product Ops + SRE 2024-12-04
- Updated with canary timelines and rollback recipes 2025-02-05

Action items (next 7 days):
- [Maya] finalize cohort list and feature flag gating (due 2024-11-15)
- [Noah] reserve dedicated pool & validate autoscale policy (due 2024-11-18)
- [Lena] add eval prompt set and baseline results to shared drive (due 2024-11-20)
- [Arjun] create alerts and link to runbook (due 2024-11-19)
- [Sofia] prepare beta customer comms and CS playbook (due 2024-11-17)

Contact / owner list: Maya Chen (product-ops), Arjun Patel (backend), Noah Kim (SRE), Lena Rodriguez (applied-ml), Sofia Martinez (CS).

End of sheet.
